ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence in accordance with the AML/CFT Act 2009 ss. 22-31, comprising: (i) screening of all directors, Ultimate Beneficial Owners, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and New Zealand sanctions instruments under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2024; (ii) mandatory screening of domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs, including family members and close associates) with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior management approval for PEP relationships, and enhanced ongoing monitoring for a minimum of 12 months; (iii) adverse media, bankruptcy, regulatory action, and financial crime watchlist review across all jurisdictions of the UBO's identity documents; (iv) reliance solely on independent, current, and verifiable identification data; and (v) mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) for any unusual activity arising during pre-incorporation onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Register (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be registered in Roman script (Latin alphabet). Names in Te Reo Maori, including macron characters, and non-Latin scripts are transliterated into Roman characters for official registration. The legal name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd', or the approved equivalent 'Tapui' for Maori-named companies, unless an exemption applies under the Companies Act 1993. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name, must not imply a connection with the Crown or Government, and must not misrepresent the company's legal form. For the International Company designator, the suffix 'International Company' or 'IC' shall be appended in accordance with the entity ELF specification.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of a name reservation, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the refusal, setting out written submissions and supporting evidence demonstrating compliance with ss. 20-21 of the Companies Act 1993. If the Registrar affirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under s. 22 of the Companies Act 1993, with the notice of appeal required under the High Court Rules 2016 to be filed within 20 working days of the reaffirmation or within such extended time as the Court may allow. Where rejection arises from a prohibited token, the applicant must first obtain the relevant ministerial or regulatory consent, including consent of the Department of Internal Affairs for gambling-related tokens under the Gambling Act 2003. A name reservation may be extended for a further 20 working days upon written application to the Companies Office before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions: New Zealand law requires a registered office to be a physical street address within New Zealand at which documents can be served and at which the share register and statutory records are physically maintained or immediately accessible; a PO Box or mail-forwarding-only service is not acceptable. A licensed virtual office service that provides a physical street address, document receipt, and records-maintenance functions is accepted by the Companies Office for a simulated social casino software publisher whose payment rails are Apple IAP and Google Play Billing. The virtual office provider must be able to produce statutory registers to the Registrar within the statutory response window, and the company must maintain a New Zealand address for service. Given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML/CFT classification, the appointed virtual office provider should be a New Zealand-incorporated company service provider subject to the AML/CFT Act 2009.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% baseline probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Companies Office within the first 12 months of incorporation; elevated to 12% if the entity becomes subject to an FMA, DIA, or NZ Police FIU risk flag or adverse media event; 20% probability of a documentary compliance review requiring production of registered office records within 5 working days.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1994 (ICA), ss 3, 7, 8, 10, 14-20 and Fourth Schedule; Companies Act 1993 (CA 1993), ss 9, 12, 122, 152, 198-199 and 238 as applied and modified by the ICA; Companies Regulations 1994; Tax Administration Act 1994, ss 39, 41 and 43; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Companies and Societies Registrar; online filing at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz; same office administers the Register of International Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an International Company (Form IC-001) and the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the New Zealand Companies Office under the International Companies Act 1994.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an International Company. The company will subscribe one ordinary share of NZ$1.00 as fully paid without any mandatory escrow account requirement. The licensed registered agent or bank custodian must nevertheless complete AML/CFT verification of source of funds before the share subscription is recorded.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE INCORPORATOR AND DIRECTOR OF [●] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Name Search and Name Reservation System (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search of the New Zealand Companies Register and relevant intellectual property registers. File Form CO-01N to reserve the proposed company name. The name must include 'Limited', 'Ltd.', or 'International Company Limited' and must not be misleading or include 'casino', 'gambling', 'bank', 'trust' or 'insurance' unless the context clearly denotes simulation, social gaming, or prior statutory authorisation. The Companies Office holds the approved name for 20 working days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CO-01N Name Reservation application
Identity documents of the name reservation applicant
Registered agent mandate letter
Written consent of the subscriber/shareholders to the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or subjected to communication, file a reconsideration request with the Registrar within 15 working days, or promptly resubmit with an alternative non-objectionable name before the reservation window lapses; the reservation fee may be transferred once upon written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional and Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand registered agent, notary public, and legal counsel (qualifications under the Law Practitioners Act 1982 and ICA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company Constitution (or adopt the default rules under the Companies Act 1993 as modified for international companies), prepare registers of members, directors and charges, obtain signed Consent to Act as Director for each director, and execute the registered office and registered agent consents. All statutory documents must be dated and signed by the incorporator(s) and each signature notarially certified or apostilled. Customer due diligence documentation under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 must be completed before the entity is presented to the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of passports of each director and significant shareholder
Proof of residential address for each director (utility bill or bank statement not older than 3 months)
Professional reference or bank reference for each director
Draft Constitution or written election to adopt statutory default rules
Form CO-02 - Director's Consent to Act
Registered office consent letter from the New Zealand registered agent
AML/CFT customer due diligence questionnaire and beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarisation is defective, obtain re-notarisation or an apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; if the Registrar or bank queries any governance document, the incorporator may execute a supplemental deed and re-file the corrected instrument with the Companies Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Issue of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) - Company Incorporation Portal and Companies Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-001 together with the approved name reservation, constitution, director consents and registered office consents, and pay the prescribed application fee. The Registrar will file the incorporation application and, if satisfied, issue a Certificate of Incorporation. The company comes into existence as a body corporate with separate legal personality and limited liability on the date specified in the certificate. The register of members must be completed showing the first allotment of the NZ$1 ordinary share.
required_dossiers: Form IC-001 - Application for Registration of an International Company
Name reservation approval reference
Executed Constitution
Form CO-02 consent for each director
Registered office consent executed by the registered agent
Share allotment record / return of allotment
Government filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a notice of proposed refusal or query, respond within 15 working days by amending the constitution, replacing a disqualified director, or changing the name. If the Registrar refuses incorporation, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for review within 20 working days after the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration and Tax-Exempt Election as an International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand; Tax Administration Act 1994
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, apply for a New Zealand IRD number using Form IR742. If the company intends to rely on its international company tax-exempt status, file the election for an international company with IRD together with a declaration that the company does not carry on business in New Zealand in the taxable sense and is beneficially owned and controlled by non-resident persons eligible under the International Companies Act 1994. The IRD will record the exemption and issue confirmation of the company's IRD number.
required_dossiers: Form IR742 - IRD number application
International company tax-exempt election form
Certificate of Incorporation
Register of directors and shareholders
Declaration of non-resident ownership and absence of New Zealand business activity
AML/CFT beneficial ownership file as accepted by the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD queries eligibility, submit a certified legal opinion and a detailed corporate and ultimate beneficial ownership chart. Where an assessment or denial is issued, file a notice of proposed adjustment/dispute within the statutory response period; if the exemption is cancelled, the board may either remedy the residency test or convert the company to an ordinary New Zealand company with full tax registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand Government — online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that derives New Zealand-source income or is required to register for GST must obtain an IRD number. Application is made via the IRD's Non-Resident Company IRD number application form (IR742) or through the myIR portal. The entity must provide certified constituent documents, proof of foreign tax residence, and details of its New Zealand business activities. IRD numbers are issued by post/fax; a non-resident company without a fixed establishment in New Zealand may also need to appoint a New Zealand agent for service of notices if carrying on a taxable activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box entity classification regime. However, an International Company incorporated under the Cook Islands International Companies Act may be treated as a non-resident company for New Zealand tax purposes if central management and control and its place of effective management are outside New Zealand. No hybrid mismatch election is generally available; New Zealand has hybrid mismatch rules (Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007) that may recharacterise payments, but no elective check-the-box mechanism exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) — value added tax (VAT-type consumption tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 turnover in any 12-month period for goods and services supplied in New Zealand by a person carrying on a taxable activity; non-resident suppliers of remote/digital services to New Zealand consumers must register under the GST on remote services rules when their taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period (no physical presence threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not require real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-approval of invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted and Peppol e-invoicing is supported voluntarily. GST returns are filed electronically via myIR on a six-monthly, two-monthly, or monthly basis depending on turnover and registration election. There is no mandatory continuous transaction controls or API clearance mechanism for invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of goods (removed from New Zealand) and to certain services supplied to non-residents who are outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not supplied in connection with land or goods in New Zealand and are not physically performed in New Zealand, or are supplied with a close connection to the recipient's business outside New Zealand. For a Cook Islands International Company with no New Zealand fixed establishment, supplies of offshore gaming services to non-resident customers would generally be outside the scope of New Zealand GST; if registered, zero-rating of exported digital/remote services may apply under section 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (NZ Customs Trade Single Window / CusMod export entry)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/forex proof of foreign currency receipt
Contract or invoice evidencing supply to a non-resident
Evidence that goods left New Zealand or services delivered offshore (e.g. IP logs, delivery records)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If a GST-registered person zero-rates an export without adequate documentation or without the foreign exchange proceeds being received within the statutory time frame, the supply is recharacterised as taxable at 15% GST, with interest and penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (e.g. late payment penalties, shortfall penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion, and use-of-money interest). Fraudulent zero-rating schemes may attract criminal penalties under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 (offence of evasion or similar), fines up to NZD 50,000 for the first offence and imprisonment in serious cases, plus retrospective clawback of any refunds and deemed taxable supply adjustments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains full IMF Article VIII status and operates a freely floating and fully convertible New Zealand dollar. No exchange control legislation restricts current account or capital account transactions, and no central bank approval is required for profit repatriation, dividend payments, royalty remittances, or equity injections. Non-resident investors may remit dividends and capital freely; any withholding taxes (e.g., non-resident dividend withholding tax or royalty withholding tax) are tax matters only and do not require foreign exchange authorization. The sole capital-control-adjacent mechanism is the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which applies to acquisitions of sensitive land and fishing quota; it does not apply to digital publishing, software licensing, or social casino game operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Reserve Bank or any mandatory conversion ratio. A New Zealand-resident exporter may retain export receipts in foreign currency accounts denominated in USD, EUR, AUD, or any other freely convertible currency without time limitation. Proceeds from digital publishing and virtual game subscriptions are treated as current account receipts and are not subject to repatriation deadlines. All cross-border receipts remain subject to standard anti-money laundering (AML) reporting obligations, including large-value transaction reporting and suspicious transaction reporting thresholds only.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not registered banks in New Zealand and cannot lawfully hold capital escrow balances in the manner of a licensed deposit-taker. They may be accepted as money remitters or payment service providers if registered under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and enrolled in the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 supervision regime. In practice, an EMI's merchant policy often prohibits or heavily restricts 'social casino' or 'virtual slots' merchants on intermediary risk grounds, and the Medium_Risk_Enhanced banking classification will trigger additional due-diligence and source-of-funds review. Therefore, EMIs may be used only for ancillary inbound/outbound settlement sweeps, not for the primary regulated treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident director of an International Company, the account opening policy of the major New Zealand registered banks generally requires either physical attendance at a New Zealand branch or a bank-approved video KYC interview. Highly rated banks permit remote onboarding only when the entity and individuals are in low-risk jurisdictions and the compliance file is complete. Due to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification of simulated social casino and virtual slots publishing, the bank will normally require at least one accountable director or beneficial owner to attend a live video or in-person interview, present an original passport, provide a notarized/certified proof of address, and execute the account mandate in person or in front of a notary. The bank may also require a legalized board resolution and a formal opinion confirming that the activity does not constitute regulated gambling under the Gambling Act 2003.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity of the Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified current extract from the International Companies registry; full register of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners; trust deed or foundation documents if a trust holds shares; management structure chart; signed statutory declarations from all natural-person beneficial owners; and evidence of tax residence of those owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perception that social casino / virtual slots operations constitute unlicensed gambling or money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from qualified New Zealand counsel confirming that the product offers no real-money wagering, no cash-out, and no exchange of winnings, and therefore falls outside the Gambling Act 2003 licensing regime; app store listing evidence through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing; in-app terms and virtual currency policy; AML risk assessment; compliance monitoring programme for player redemptions and token transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for inbound capital injection from non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements covering at least 12 months for each funding entity; audited financial statements of the parent or investor; signed source-of-wealth declaration; evidence of underlying corporate earnings or sale of assets; tax clearance certificates from the remitting jurisdiction; explanation of the commercial rationale for the investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or PEP-linked counterparty exposure in the gaming value chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and adverse-media screening reports for all directors and shareholders; independent relationship review from a law firm or licensed accountant; jurisdictional risk assessment of all counterparties and vendor payees; enhanced transaction monitoring commitment; documented rationale for any jurisdiction considered high-risk.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the parent or investor's bank to the International Company's New Zealand settlement account. Use the cross-border purpose code consistent with equity capital contribution (e.g., OECD BPM6 'Shares and other equity - credit') and include a clear narrative such as 'Capital Contribution for ISIC 5820 Software Publishing'. The receiving bank will require the board resolution authorizing the share allotment, the updated share register, disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owner, and evidence that the funds derive from legitimate sources. Because the business is software publishing and digital game distribution, no consent under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 is required; however, if the company later purchases real estate or fishing quota in New Zealand, the relevant OIA approval must be obtained before completion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound B2B disbursements for licensing fees, cloud server hosting, editorial services, marketing, and software development are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments. For New Zealand domestic vendor settlements, the bank may use the local bulk electronic clearing system (BECS) or host-to-host NZD payments. For high-value supply contracts involving game development or media licensing, a commercial letter of credit (MT700) can be used against invoice, shipping, or acceptance documents when contractually required. Winnings or payouts to players must never be routed through these clearing rails, as the social casino model is non-cash-out and non-real-money; any such payment would undermine the legal opinion that the product is not regulated gambling.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies that cannot be delivered onshore
FX swaps for short-term rolling of foreign currency inflows to NZD
Cross-currency swaps for long-term funding or intercompany loan hedging
Plain vanilla currency options for revenue downside protection on non-NZD app store proceeds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Companies Office Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s. 204)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 30 working days after the company's annual return date, being the anniversary of incorporation or an alternative date fixed by board resolution; periodical re-filing is annual on the same return date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registrar issues a default notice; failure to remedy within 20 working days triggers a Gazette strike-off notice and dissolution of the company. Continuing offence carries a daily penalty of NZD 10 per director (max NZD 1,000) under s. 212; the company is also locked out of filing other registry documents (e.g., other registry documents) and a director may be disqualified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return and Terminal/Provisional Tax Payment (IR4)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due 7 July following the tax year (non-standard balance date: 7th day of the 4th month after balance date); with an approved tax agent extension the filing deadline is 31 March of the following year; terminal tax is due 7 February for a standard balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 100 immediately plus NZD 100 per day up to 50 days (aggregate cap NZD 5,000); late payment penalty 1% of the unpaid amount immediately and a further 4% after 7 days; prescribed interest (use-of-money) accrues on underpayments at 8.39% p.a.; evasion penalties up to 150% of shortfall may apply for deliberate misreporting. A tax-exempt non-resident IC with no New Zealand-source income is not required to file a return and no sanction arises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST Return (IR301 / IR302) — only if GST-registered; digital gaming sales via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing in New Zealand are subject to GST at 15% for supplies to NZ-resident consumers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six-monthly filers: returns for the 1 April–30 September and 1 October–31 March periods are due by 7 November and 7 May respectively; two-monthly filers: returns due by the 28th (or 7th if filing online) of the month following the end of the taxable period; a taxpayer on the six-monthly basis may elect monthly filings if refunds are frequently claimed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty NZD 50 per return where the return is filed late and the GST payable exceeds NZD 100; late payment penalty 1% immediately and a further 4% after day 7; plus statutory interest on unpaid GST at the prescribed rate; persistent non-filing can trigger an IRD default assessment and debt collection enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) reconciliation and dividend-related declarations (IR4W / IR46), if the IC distributes profits to non-resident shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: NRWT is paid on the 20th day of the month following the month of dividend payment; the annual reconciliation is lodged together with the IR4 annual return (due 7 July or 31 March with agent extension as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty 1% plus 4% after 7 days; use-of-money interest on unpaid NRWT; failure to withhold correctly exposes the paying company to a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the underpaid amount in cases of intentional under-withholding; IRD can issue binding rulings and audit the WHT position.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Companies Act 1993 (ss. 196–207D) and the Financial Reporting Act 2013, an independent audit is compulsory for: (1) FMC reporting entities under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; (2) large companies with total assets exceeding NZD 60 million or total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million; (3) companies that elect or are required by a 5%-independent-shareholder audit request (s. 199); and (4) overseas-incorporated companies with a New Zealand place of business that would qualify as large. Small companies (total assets not exceeding NZD 3 million and revenue not exceeding NZD 6 million) are fully exempt from audit and financial-statements filing; a simulated social casino publisher with app-store-only models and offshore passive revenue will normally fall below all thresholds and requires no audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (Tier 1) for public accountability entities; NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2) for large non-publicly-accountable entities; NZ Simplified Accounting Standard (Tier 3) and NZ Special Accounting Framework (Tier 4) for small companies, as prescribed by the External Reporting Board (XRB). For a tax-exempt International Company that is non-resident in New Zealand and does not carry on a business there, the annual accounts may be prepared under the foreign GAAP agreed with the parent/beneficial owner (e.g., US GAAP or IFRS) and, absent a New Zealand filing obligation, no XRB framework is mandatory.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand currently has no public UBO filing for ordinary or international companies. The Companies Act 1993 requires a register of members to be updated within 10 working days of a share transfer; the licensed registered agent performs an annual due-diligence refresh of beneficial ownership under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and retains a signed UBO confirmation on file (no Companies Office lodgement). The Companies (Reporting of Beneficial Ownership) Amendment Bill 2024, when brought into force, will require beneficial-ownership disclosure to the Registrar for overseas companies holding land or carrying on business in New Zealand; the CK_IC's non-resident tax-exempt structure will be captured only once the validating regulations are gazetted for the simulation period. Shareholder resolutions and register consents are tabled in the minute book at the annual shareholding meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registered ownership and share transfers)
Register of Directors (names, residential addresses, service addresses, and dates of appointment)
Minute Book (board and shareholder resolutions and decision logs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–650 for a standard innovative startup registered-office-plus-agent retainer at a New Zealand company service provider; full corporate-secretarial service including annual return lodgement, register maintenance, and AML/CFT UBO refresh is USD 900–1,900
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit or review engagement is mandated for a small non-listed social-casino publisher; if an audit is required voluntarily (for overseas parent consolidation or a bank requirement), a third-tier registered chartered accounting firm will quote USD 2,000–5,000 for a single-entity IC with simple revenue streams; a limited review engagement would price at USD 1,200–2,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory imputation regime and R&D tax credit (15% of eligible expenditure); qualifying International Company (exempt-zone) status may exempt certain foreign-sourced income and non-resident profits from New Zealand corporate tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Tax Return filed through Inland Revenue myIR portal (electronic filing; paper IR4 accepted only in exceptional circumstances)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the return is due on 7 July if filed online, or 30 June for paper returns; for non-standard balance dates, the due date is the last day of the fourth month after balance date (electronic) or third month after balance date (paper). Tax agents may obtain an extension of time to 31 March of the following income year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all New Zealand-sourced income; foreign income only if derived through a New Zealand permanent establishment or taxed under New Zealand law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses incurred in deriving assessable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only allowable deductions directly connected to New Zealand-source income, on an arm's length basis; no deduction for artificial, circular, or round-trip payments to associated entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Net profit is the starting point for tax; a loss must satisfy shareholder continuity and business integrity tests before carry-forward is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carried forward from prior years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a continuity schedule; the same 49% ultimate New Zealand resident shareholder continuity must be maintained from the loss year to the offset year.
The amount chargeable after loss offsets; non-resident companies are taxed at the 28% corporate rate on this amount.
Apply the statutory 28% rate to Box 5; include any RWT, FDP, or NRWT credits already withheld by New Zealand payers.
Non-resident shareholders cannot use imputation credits unless they file a New Zealand return with a permanent establishment; complete schedule IR45B.
Indicate final amount due to Inland Revenue or refundable; refunds to non-residents are issued only after verification of tax residence and beneficial ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty (LFP) of NZ$250 immediately, increasing by NZ$250 if the return remains outstanding one month after the due date; late payment penalty of 1% on the day after the due date, rising to 4% seven days later, plus use-of-money interest (currently approximately 10.45% for underpayments) accruing daily until payment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-residents; fully imputed dividends may attract no additional NRWT where the supplementary dividend regime is used; DTA relief may reduce the residual rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA, the non-resident payee must obtain a New Zealand IRD 902 tax residence confirmation (or an equivalent Certificate of Residence from the treaty jurisdiction) and provide it to the New Zealand paying company before the dividend, interest, or royalty is paid. The payer then applies the reduced DTA rate at source. If over-withheld, the non-resident must file a New Zealand IR4 or IR3 return within the statutory four-year refund window and attach the TRC, a statement of beneficial ownership, and documentary evidence of the underlying transaction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic NRWT is 15% for both royalties and interest. Under most New Zealand DTAs the rates are reduced to 10% for interest and royalties; certain treaties contemplate nil or 5% rates for specific categories, subject to beneficial-ownership, anti-conduit, and transaction-substance conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZ$1 million: cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZ$1 million in an income year require contemporaneous Local File documentation; multinational groups with consolidated global revenue of NZ$1.3 billion or more additionally require a Master File and Country-by-Country Report filed with Inland Revenue.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) code; nonetheless, economic substance is embedded in the general anti-avoidance rules, the permanent establishment definition, and DTA entitlement tests. A Cook Islands / foreign International Company or other shell that cannot demonstrate real management, employees, premises, and decision-making in New Zealand will be denied New Zealand tax residence, treaty certificates, and may be subject to reconstruction assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Apple IAP/Google Play gross sales, using false invoice deductions, suppressing non-resident distribution income, or creating fictitious costs to reduce taxable income in the IR4 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under ss 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994; imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to NZ$50,000 for individuals and NZ$200,000 for companies; civil shortfall penalties up to 100% of the tax evaded, plus late payment penalties and use-of-money interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly signs a false return is an accessory and may be personally assessed for the full shortfall, disqualified from managing companies for up to 5 years, subjected to asset preservation orders, face cancellation of New Zealand travel arrangements while serving sentence, and be extradited in cases of cross-border fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring related-party payments for game development, IP licensing, marketing, or data services at non-arm's length amounts, especially to a zero-rated Cook Islands International Company, to erode New Zealand taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may reconstruct the transaction under ss GC 6–GC 14, impose transfer pricing penalties up to 100% of the shortfall (or 40% for failing to maintain prescribed documentation), and apply anti-avoidance penalties; interest accrues from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the mispriced arrangement are jointly and severally liable for corporate taxes where the company is a mere conduit or facade; they may face personal penalty assessments, director disqualification, and, if knowingly assisting fraud, criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the CK_IC International Company corporate shell without office, employees, contracts, or economic activity to obtain New Zealand tax-exempt status, treaty certificates, or to avoid the economic-substance requirements applicable to digital gaming royalties and dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA relief; assessment of 28% corporate tax on all income; imposition of anti-avoidance penalties; the shell may be struck off under the Companies Act 1993 for no real business; promoters and advisers are also liable for penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the company is a facade, courts may pierce the veil and hold the controlling director personally liable for unpaid tax, interest, and penalties; a travel restriction order may be issued while tax debts are outstanding, and directors face civil restitution and up to 5 years' imprisonment for fraudulent misuse of exempt-zone status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Compliance Failure (Virtual Currency and IAP Railing)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Apple App Store / Google Play payments for simulated casino tokens without carrying out customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, or suspicious activity reporting, with deliberate concealment from the Financial Intelligence Unit under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil liability up to NZ$2 million for a reporting entity; criminal penalties for individuals up to NZ$300,000 and for bodies corporate up to NZ$4 million per breach; revocation of operating licenses; asset forfeiture and restraint orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the reporting entity can be prosecuted personally where AML failures are systemic or reckless; each director faces fines, disqualification from managing any financial institution and, in cases of money-laundering facilitation, imprisonment up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeatedly ignoring statutory IR4 deadlines, refusing access to accounting records for Apple/Google billing statements, or destroying evidence during an Inland Revenue audit of the tax-exempt shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic late filing penalties and late payment penalties, plus shortfall penalties for obstruction of 20%–100% of tax; every non-compliant year is assessed separately; Inland Revenue can obtain a production order and issue a non-compliance notification that blocks online government services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Failure to file is a strict liability offence; the director who controls the accounting function is liable for penalty fines and compromised data-access bans; where the failure is deliberate evasion, the director may be imprisoned and disqualified from serving as a director of any New Zealand company.
